findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing only `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. This is a gitlink (submodule pointer), not source code, and appears unrelated to the feature. Unless intentionally adding a submodule, this should be removed: it can break fresh clones/CI and will pin or update the parent repository unexpectedly.

findings.title: Naive substring check misclassifies mixed/negated error queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query()` does a raw substring search for `event.type:error`. Queries such as `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` contain that substring, so an allowlisted project on the discover dataset will be treated as error-focused and `count()` will be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`. Transactions either lack usable sample_weight or should be counted separately, so counts become wrong or the query fails. The filter must be parsed/validated to ensure the query actually selects only error events (for example, no negation or OR-mixing with transactions).

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` passes the outer `dataset` from the request, not the `scoped_dataset` that is actually being queried. For dashboard split logic this function is called with `split_dataset=discover` (and modified queries), while the outer dataset can be metrics/performance. The helper then evaluates against the wrong dataset and the original request query, so the split errors-only query can skip upsampling or be misclassified. Pass `scoped_dataset` and the local `query` down so the decision matches the query actually executed.
